title: Using a stack: evaluate a postfix expression
summary: In 2 3 * 5 4 * +, each operator works on the last two numbers. A stack keeps them in the right order.

checkpoints.text: A digit is pushed. `c - '0'` turns the character '2' into the number 2.
The first operator, `*`. The two numbers on top of the stack are popped: 3 (right) and then 2 (left).
2 * 3 = 6 is pushed back. The stack now holds one number, the value of everything read so far.
At `+`, the stack held 6 and 20 (from 5 * 4): exactly the two operands. 20 has just been popped as the right one; 6 comes next.
26, which is 2 * 3 + 5 * 4. Postfix needs no brackets and no precedence rules; calculators and compilers use this idea.
